narrative.overview:
Chinni Treasure looks like a jeweller's workbench after closing time. The surface is dark and quiet — lacquer black, warm cream, a single precious metal — and the only thing that moves is light passing over gold. Nothing shouts. The gold appears in small, deliberate amounts: a 48px rule beneath a heading, a hairline under the navbar, a border that warms when you hover. Its scarcity is the point.

Restraint carries the luxury because the price point cannot. At under ₹5,000, this is not a watch-company vault; it is a craft studio that has decided its work deserves to be presented properly. So craft is shown rather than claimed — large photography, generous whitespace, and a serif with real drawn contrast doing the talking. The body copy stays quiet and small; the eye should land on the object, not the sentence about the object.

Warmth is engineered into the mechanics. Everything you can touch lifts two pixels and settles back when pressed. Gold controls catch a diagonal shimmer. This is warmth through the hands rather than through exclamation marks, which is what keeps 'Little Love' from tipping into sentimentality.
keyCharacteristics: Gold is a punctuation mark, never a paragraph
Dark surfaces, cream content — the room is dim, the work is lit
Uppercase micro-labels with wide tracking open every section
Photography is the largest element on any product surface
Motion is slow on entry and instant on response

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Gold appears on roughly a tenth of any given screen. Its rarity is the entire point — a page where gold is everywhere reads cheap, and cheap contradicts everything the brand claims.

rules.name: The Dark Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold text on cream backgrounds uses --gold-deep, never --gold. The brighter gold fails WCAG AA 4.5:1 against a light ground, and luxury that nobody can read is not luxury.

rules.name: The Three-Weight Rule
rules.body: Typography runs at three weights only — 300/400 light for serif display, 500/600 for sans labels and body. Nothing heavier, ever. Weight is not how this system creates emphasis; space and gold are.

rules.name: The Script Restriction Rule
rules.body: Pinyon Script is a signature, not a typeface. It appears only in the footer wordmark and the 'Little Love' tagline. It never touches a heading, body copy, form label, or price.

rules.name: The Lift-and-Settle Rule
rules.body: Every interactive element lifts translateY(-2px) on hover and presses to translateY(1px) scale(0.985) on active. If something can be touched, it does this. Static interactivity is the fastest way to make a craft store feel like a template.

rules.name: The Ambient Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are gold-warm and atmospheric, never neutral-grey and structural. A shadow's job is to catch the light in the room, not to explain the stacking order.

rules.name: The Near-Sharp Corner Rule
rules.body: Corners stay between 2px and 8px. Nothing is fully square and nothing is pill-shaped, except true pills like badges and quantity controls. Soft-round reads friendly-consumer; fully square reads brutalist. This is neither.

dos: Do use --gold-deep for any text on cream or white.
Do keep photography at 4:5 aspect and let it be the largest thing in the card.
Do pair every section heading with the 48px gold rule.
Do lift on hover and press on active for anything clickable.
Do let the serif carry headlines and the sans carry everything functional.
Do preserve visible focus rings at 3px gold-tinted spread.
donts: Don't use --gold for body text on light backgrounds — it fails contrast.
Don't add a second accent hue; the single-gold discipline is the system.
Don't set copy in Pinyon Script outside the footer wordmark.
Don't introduce heavy font weights (700+) to create emphasis.
Don't use fully square (0px) or pill (999px) corners on cards and buttons.
Don't add feature CSS to app/globals.css — new styles belong in their own module under app/styles/ and are wired through @import.
